jobs.occupation: Senior Advisor Human Rights (m/f/d) (Amtsanwalt/-anwältin)
jobs.description: Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:The Senior Advisor Human Rights provides strategic and technical leadership for Fairtrade International’s human rights agenda. The role leads the implementation and continued development of Fairtrade’s Human Rights Risk and Remediation Strategy and Human Rights Theory of Change, ensuring alignment with international human rights standards and evolving HREDD expectations.The role combines strategic leadership with hands-on expertise in human rights risk management, complex case management, remediation and crisis response. It also plays a key role in strengthening human rights capabilities across the Fairtrade system and represents Fairtrade externally on human rights matters.The focus will be on: Strategy, Risk & Governance- Lead Fairtrade’s human rights agenda and act as its senior technical authority on human rights.- Implement and further develop the Human Rights Risk and Remediation Strategy and Theory of Change.- Advise Executive Leadership and relevant governance bodies on significant risks, emerging issues and strategic priorities.- Strengthen human rights risk identification, assessment and management across Fairtrade contexts.- Translate international standards and regulatory developments into practical approaches for producer and supply-chain contexts.Case Management, Remediation & Crisis Response- Oversee the management, escalation, remediation and closure of human rights allegations and violations.- Provide expert leadership on complex, sensitive and high-risk cases, ensuring an affected-person-centred, rights-based and safeguarding-conscious approach.- Strengthen case-management processes, escalation pathways, governance and monitoring of remediation.- Lead the continued digitalisation of Fairtrade’s human rights case-management system, including appropriate confidentiality and data-protection safeguards.- Provide senior human rights expertise during serious incidents and crises.System Coordination & Capacity BuildingWorking closely with Fairtrade Africa, NAPP, CLAC, National Fairtrade Organisations, FLOCERT, Producer Organisations and the HREDD Center of Excellence the advisor will:- Promote consistency, knowledge sharing and cross-regional learning while enabling appropriate local adaptation.- Lead capacity building through training, guidance, tools, workshops and knowledge-sharing initiatives.- Strengthen the ability of regional and local teams to implement Fairtrade’s human rights approaches effectively. Stakeholder Engagement & Representation- Represent Fairtrade International with governments, civil society, international organisations, businesses and other stakeholders.- Communicate complex human rights issues clearly to senior leadership, Producer Organisations and external audiences.- Build constructive dialogue across diverse stakeholders and contribute to relevant international and multi-stakeholder forums.- Support communications and media engagement on sensitive or high-profile human rights matters when required.Monitoring & Learning- Monitor implementation and effectiveness of Fairtrade’s human rights work and progress against the Theory of Change.- Capture and apply learning from cases, remediation, stakeholder engagement and regional implementation.- Monitor developments in human rights law, responsible business conduct and HREDD regulation and assess their implications for Fairtrade.SKILLS REQUIRED:Level of education: Advanced degree in International Law, Human Rights, Public International Law or a related discipline; legal training/qualification is strongly preferred.Years of professional experience: more than 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in human rights, responsible business conduct, international development, labour rights, human rights due diligence, access to remedy or closely related fields.Language requirements: Fluency in English, knowledge of relevant languages to Fairtrade producer regions is desirable.  Knowledge / Job Specific Competencies:Job-specific- Risk Management- Crisis Management- Stakeholder Management- Capacity Building- International Development Expertise- Supply Chain Knowledge- Strategic Planning- Compliance Management- Ability to engage and influence stakeholders Personal qualities- Analytical Thinking- Problem-Solving- Diplomacy- Integrity- Influence- Relationship Management- Collaboration / Teamwork- Cross-Cultural Communication- Cultural Adaptability- EmpathyTERMS AND CONDITIONS:- This is a full-time position within Fairtrade International.- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements- The office language is English.- Salary as per the Collective Bargaining Agreement for the Wholesale and Foreign Trade Industries for North Rhine Westphalia Group VIb and over tariff payments,starting from €5975.2 gross per month- Holiday Bonus and 13th salary  - 30 days of holidays per year (for fulltime employees)- Subsidised public transportation ticket- Subsidised meal services- Childcare cost subsidyPlease note that Fairtrade International is strict on compliance with the required qualification criteria mentioned above, and only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

jobs.occupation: Technical assistant (m/f/d) (16/2026) (Biologisch-technische/r Assistent/in)
jobs.description: Your area of responsibility Research topic: Plant immunity Plant pathogens secrete small molecules in their host to manipulate cellular processes and cause disease. Plants are not defenseless, however, and have evolved a wide variety of immune receptors to sense these pathogen-associated molecules and subsequently trigger an immune response to restrict pathogen infection. In the Molecular Plant Immunity research group, we investigate the molecular basis of effector recognition and immune receptor activation, and how evolutionary forces shape these processes. We then leverage this knowledge to develop strategies for sustainable disease resistance in crops. jobs.occupation: Doctoral researcher (m/f/d/x) in geography – Assessing socio-economic impacts of climate extremes (Geograf/in)
jobs.description: Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Institute for Geography at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences seeks to fill the above position.The PhD position is part of the project “CASCADE – Cascading impacts of climate extremes: new perspectives for interlinking Earth System Sciences in Leipzig” on compound and cascading impacts of climate extremes. CASCADE investigates how floods and droughts affect society and the environment, combining large-scale data analysis with a systems perspective on human–environment interactions.Our knowledge of the impacts of climate extremes is only as good as the data that record them. The PhD project aims to uncover biases in climate impact databases and research and to provide a more comprehensive view of flood and drought impacts at the global scale. To this end, the doctoral researcher will link and harmonise existing databases (e.g. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, EM-DAT) into a common event, impact and spatial framework, and will contribute to developing a multilingual news-based impact dataset that helps to fill gaps in existing sources. Using independent global hazard and exposure data as a reference, the project will analyse where and for which impacts the sources agree, how reported magnitudes differ, and how the likelihood that an event is recorded at all depends on hazard severity, exposure, socioeconomic conditions, language and media presence.The project benefits from close collaboration with the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ). The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team at the interface of geography, climate-risk research and data science.About the position- Salary group 13  TV-L - Fixed term of 3 years, Qualification-related purposes - 75 % of a full-time position, part-time employment possible- Start date: 1 March 2027The role- Linking and harmonisation of text-based and established impact databases (e.g. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, news-based data, EM-DAT) into a common global event, impact and spatial framework- Comparative analysis of where, when and for which impact types the datasets converge or diverge, using global hazard and exposure data as an independent reference- Analysis of the geographical, socioeconomic and linguistic factors that shape the visibility of impacts in different data sources- Development of a combined, bias-aware global view of flood and drought impacts- Contribution to the development and validation of a multilingual news-based impact dataset using natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs)- Publication of results in international peer-reviewed journals, presentation at scientific conferences and open publication of code and dataAbout you- University degree (e.g. master’s) or equivalent in geography, computational social sciences, digital humanities, environmental or earth system sciences, disaster risk research or a closely related field- Experience in data analysis, in particular in combining and harmonising heterogeneous datasets, e.g. demonstrated through the master’s thesis, research projects or work experience- Excellent programming skills (e.g. Python, R)- Experience in the analysis of spatial data, e.g. spatial statistics- Interest in climate-risk, natural-hazard or disaster research, e.g. demonstrated through coursework or the master’s thesis- Very good written and spoken English (at least language proficiency level B2)- Experience with, or demonstrable interest in, natural language processing or large language models preferable, e.g. through coursework or projectsWhat we offer you- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working life, with opportunities for continuing professional development- a wide range of occupational health management services - Remuneration in line with the collective bargaining agreement of the federal states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. If you have any questions about accessibility or need assistance with this application process, please contact Leipzig University’s disability officers at: schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de (https://mailto:schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de) .Have we sparked your interest?Please submit your application addressed to Prof. Dr. Miguel Mahecha, Institute’s Director, by 23 November 2026 via our online application portal (https://uni-leipzig.b-ite.careers/en/jobposting/68a780049a96ddf8d6fa4bea19873171c42d4e1f0/apply) .Your application should include:Cover letter; CV; copies of degree certificates and transcripts; a research statement (max. 2 pages) outlining how the applicant would approach combining impact datasets and identifying their biases and blind spots; summary or excerpt from your master’s thesis or another writing sample; contact details of two refereesIf you have any questions about the role, please contact Prof. Dr. Mariana Madruga de Brito, Professor, 0341 60252149.
